Remaining declaration-ish nodes — type_parameter_list (generics bounds), function_type (callback types) — are parsed but not emitted as standalone symbols; they are structural, not declaration sites. differential go-tools:go is 0 missing / 0 unexplained at the pinned floor; at FULL extent (#914 round, script/m14/tmp/go-799-surface.ts and script/m14/tmp/go-914-sweep.ts) go-tools reads 1,931 files / truth 30,695 / MISSING 0 / unexplained 0, terraform 1,993 files / truth 40,913 / MISSING 0 / unexplained 0, and kubernetes 13,488 files / MISSING 0 / unexplained 0 in four index-range chunks with 0 parse skips — the 10+2 and 22 name-only `implements` rows GO24 describes are gone, not rounded away. analyzer literals that are structural-internal (func_type/function_type, string_literal/interpreted_string_literal) are internal_silent by contract.

gaps.statement: Two LEGAL Go constructs have no representation in the pinned tree-sitter-go grammar — a package-scope generic function VALUE and a method on an INSTANTIATED GENERIC RECEIVER — and error recovery swallows the declarations that follow: 3 of 1,931 go-tools files, 92 declarations, 0 of 1,993 terraform files. Those declarations are not symbols and carry no `contains` edges in either direction.

The round fixed what it CAN fix (the fabricated construction, GO15), and pinned that the loss STOPS at the declaration: the calls inside a recovered body are published again (GO16). Fixture go/grammar-error-not-a-construction-889 deliberately does NOT assert the swallowed `caller` symbol, and go/error-region-callee-descend-799 asserts the calls without asserting the recovered declarations as symbols.

gaps.kind: declared precision residue on the `uses` surface (NOT hidable, NOT a coverage gap)
gaps.statement: With `uses` in go's compared-label set, the round-6 truth agrees with the analyzer on 154,656 of 154,660 rows across 5 corpora / 6,825 files: 0 MISSING and 4 EXTRA (0.0026%). All four are the ANALYZER publishing a read the truth does not derive, i.e. the analyzer is a strict superset on this surface and no read is hidden. They are two shapes, both in `testdata/` fixtures written to exercise mutation analysis rather than to be read: (1) three `go_selector_use` rows in go/analysis/passes/modernize/testdata/src/slicesbackward/slicesbackward.go, targets `items`, `n`, `inner`, where the field appears in a position the truth classifies as a write or an address-of (`s[i].n = 5`, `s[i].n++`, `_ = &s[i].n`) and the analyzer counts the field visit regardless; (2) one `identifier_usage` row in gopls/internal/analysis/unusedparams/testdata/src/a/a.go line 79, `uses _ -> y`, where `y` is a parameter name in a function TYPE (`var fib func(x, y int) int`) — a declaration the analyzer reads as a bare identifier because the name is in file scope.
gaps.why_it_is_not_just_fixed: Shape (1) is a judgement about whether an address-taken or incremented field is a read; the truth says no for a pure write, the analyzer says the field was visited. Shape (2) is 1 row in 6,825 files and was not reproducible in a minimal file during this round, so a fix for it would be a guess rather than a repair. Both are recorded with their exact file and line so the next round can settle them with a fixture instead of a corpus count. Neither can mask a missing read, and the round-6 full-extent read shows no MISSING anywhere on the surface.

decisions.node_type: interface implementation
decisions.question: Go uses implicit interface satisfaction (duck typing), not explicit implements clauses.
decisions.resolution: The analyzer derives implements from method-set matching (all interface methods present on the struct's receiver set); no explicit `implements`/`: I` clause exists in the grammar. The oracle (deriveGoImplements) mirrors this name-set check.

decisions.node_type: struct embedding / calls
decisions.question: Struct embedding (anonymous fields) is Go's composition mechanism; bare-callee calls must resolve to in-file declared functions/methods.
decisions.resolution: Embedded anonymous fields emit one extends edge (family composition contract, no contains twin). Calls use leaf targets; bare identifiers emit only when they name an in-file declared function/method (type conversions string(x)/float64(x) and closure vars are NOT call truth).

decisions.node_type: callback/closure semantics
decisions.question: Anonymous func_literal bodies and goroutine/defer closures have no static callable name.
decisions.resolution: func_literal in call position emits NO calls target (no static name, same class as Rust's (self.0)); goroutine/defer handler emits only named leaf callees that resolve to a declared function/method. Scope tied to the pinned tree-sitter-go grammar.

decisions.node_type: selector field uses: assignment-LHS writes; interface embedding extends
decisions.question: M37 #604 dual-lens (go-tools + terraform, 3,924 files): (a) analyzeGoSelectorUses emitted `uses` for assignment-LHS field WRITES and inc/dec operands — 5,202 write-only (fn, field) bogus edges; the family write-gate (cpp/c/php/ruby/python/groovy/objc/ts) was missing in go. (b) `interface { Reader; io.Closer }` emitted only a member-symbol contains, never an inheritance edge — 156 embedding sites; struct embedding already gave extends, java/rust give superinterfaces extends.
decisions.resolution: (a) write-gate: a selector whose parent is the FIRST expression_list child of an assignment_statement (`=` AND `+=` — both writes per SCD1 family parity) or an inc/dec_statement operand emits no uses; chained operand reads (`r.cfg` inside `r.cfg.V = v`) stay genuine reads. (b) interface embedding emits extends to the type LEAF (Reader, Closer) with relationshipType go_interface_embedding, mirroring go_struct_embedding and the rust trait-supertrait/java interface-extends contract. Both mirrored in the oracle; pinned by relationship-and-payloads (persist->writeOnly forbid) and implements-params (ReadCloser->Reader go_interface_embedding).

decisions.node_type: implements: non-struct method-bearing types, named-result signatures, generics
decisions.question: M37 #604 dual-lens implements gaps on go-tools @200 (6 MISSING): (a) only isStruct symbols were checked as implementors, so `type HandlerFunc func(...)` / `type subcommands []command` with methods never satisfied interfaces (jsonrpc2 HandlerFunc/PreempterFunc, gopls subcommands); (b) the raw-text result signature compare treated named results `(result any, err error)` as different from unnamed `(any, error)` (defaultHandler vs Handler/Preempter); (c) generic receivers `MapLattice[Key, Elem, L]` never matched the declared name; and the name-only oracle over-claimed function-local (`interface hasCommands` in a func body) and generic-instantiation (MapLattice -> Semilattice[map[Key]Elem]) pairs.
decisions.resolution: Analyzer: implementor candidates now include all non-interface declared types (Struct + Type); result extraction reduces named-result parameter_lists to canonical TYPE text (`T` / `(T1, T2)`); receivers strip generic brackets `[`. Oracle mirrors: receiver strip `[`/`<`, no descent into function/method/func_literal bodies (LocalsAreNotSymbols), and generic type_spec pairs are skipped on BOTH sides (satisfaction needs type unification — refusal over fabrication). Pinned by implements-params (RunnerFn->Runner2, HandlerImpl->NamedResulter, Box->GenericIface forbid). go-tools @200 and terraform @120 both 100%/0/0.

decisions.node_type: composite-literal construction instantiates
decisions.question: M37 #604: Go's primary construction syntax `Foo{...}` / `&Foo{...}` / `pkg.Foo{...}` emitted NO instantiates — only NewXxx calls did (65,843 composite literals across go-tools+terraform with zero construction edges). Rust emits instantiates for struct literals, csharp for `new Foo()` — family parity gap.
decisions.resolution: New analyzeGoCompositeLiteralConstruction emits instantiates (go_composite_literal_construction) sourced to the containing fn/method ("global" at package scope) with the literal's type LEAF as target; slice/map/array literals (wrapper type child) and elided element literals (no type child) are skipped. Stored package-scope closures are NOT descended (template, not run at init — mirrors the package-scope call contract); local closures inside bodies keep the enclosing fn. Oracle mirrored; pinned by relationship-and-payloads (NewShape->Shape, work->Worker composite pins).

decisions.node_type: framework detection (import-path based)
decisions.question: M37 #604 wave-2 (RSD7 lesson carried from rust wave-6): framework truth is differential-invisible — deriveGoEdges derives no framework truth — and NO go fixture pinned detectedFrameworks, so dropping detection could never fail a gate. The go analyzer detects frameworks from canonical import paths only (gin/echo/fiber/net_http/gorilla_mux/grpc/testify — deterministic, zero code string-matching). Verified on go-tools+terraform (3,924 files): net_http 86, grpc 50, zero false positives. Now fixture-gated: framework-detection.go asserts the EXACT set [gin, net_http, gorilla_mux, grpc] plus constructor-call/composite-literal pins, and mutant go/drop-framework-detection dies.
decisions.ruling: FIXED — import-path framework detection is genuine (net_http/grpc hits verified against real imports in go-tools); no false positives on either corpus. Fixture framework-detection.go + 272nd mutant now gate it permanently.

decisions.node_type: channel send/receive/select uses (go_channel_operation)
decisions.question: M37 #604 wave-3 (full read of analyzeGoSpecificPatterns + extractGoChannelVariable): channel-op uses were differential-INVISIBLE (uses is NOT in go's compared-label set; deriveGoEdges derives no uses truth) and pinned nowhere, so two defects ran uncaught: (a) NO dedup — every send site pushed a row, 79 duplicate (fn,channel,direction) rows across go-tools+terraform; (b) RAW OPERAND TEXT targets — member channels as dotted `h.jobs`, method-result channels as `ctx.Done()` (a call!), bare locals/params as `c` (LocalsAreNotSymbols), 327 garbage/non-leaf targets. Family contract: uses targets = declared leaf names only. Ruling: channel ops emit ONE deduped uses row per (fn, channel-leaf, direction) ONLY when the operand resolves to a declared channel — bare package-scope var/const (27/160 bare identifiers measured) or a member selector (leaf + send/receive direction, owned by the channel pass; the selector pass skips channel operands so members get one row not two). Bare locals/params, anonymous channels, and call results emit NOTHING. Parse shapes probe-verified: communication_case wraps receive_statement > unary_expression, so send/receive/unary branches cover select cases (no separate case branch — pre-fix double-counted).
decisions.ruling: FIXED — corpus: 79 dup rows -> 0, 327 garbage targets -> 0, 109 files with channel uses -> 50. type-usage-graph fixture pins worker->jobs(send+receive)/doneAll(receive) channel ops + forbids pump->ch/done locals and dotted h.jobs; 273rd mutant go/reemit-dotted-channel-uses dies. 4/4 go fixtures, differential go-tools @60 100%/0/0.

decisions.node_type: qualified_calls payload dedup
decisions.question: M37 #604 wave-3 (payload audit of qualified_calls on go-tools+terraform): findGoFunctionCalls pushed one entry per CALL SITE with no dedup — a function calling the same callee N times carried N identical entries (29,463 excess rows on 4,719 symbols; total 103,339 -> 73,876 entries after fix). The rust #383 lesson: qualified_calls is a UNIQUE set of callee paths per function symbol (rust dedupes at attach with [...new Set()]). Chain-call forms like `time.Now().Format` and `exec.Command(...).CombinedOutput` are NOT junk — rust parity keeps full chain paths (`String::from("x").trim().to_uppercase`); only the duplicate multiplicity was wrong.
decisions.ruling: FIXED — findGoFunctionCalls dedupes via a seen set; corpus 4,719 dup symbols -> 0, 29,463 excess rows removed. relationship-and-payloads fixture pins startWork countEquals s.startWork:1 (two self-call sites: go + defer); 274th mutant go/duplicate-qualified-calls dies. Fixtures 4/4 go, differential go-tools @60 100%/0/0.

decisions.node_type: assignment LHS write gate
decisions.question: Go second review (2026-09-13): every side of every assignment wraps in expression_list, so the direct-parent LHS check never fired and every written name leaked as a use whenever it resolved (probe: `a, b = 1, 2` with no reads at all emitted f->a, f->b; even single `a = 1` leaked).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: climb through expression_lists only — landing in the first-child subtree of an assignment_statement is a write, stopping anywhere else (index/call/selector/unary) is a read; `=` and `+=` both write (selector-pass parity). Fixture forbids writeonly->wa/wb and writeplain->wa; mutant go/assign-lhs-reads CAUGHT.

decisions.node_type: parameter binding granularity
decisions.question: Go second review (2026-09-13): parameter binding swallowed whole subtrees, so an array length (`f(a [N]int)`) bound the file const N and suppressed the genuine `return N` read (probe-verified missing pair).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: bind leading name identifiers only (Go params are names-first; `a, b int` binds both, `f(int)` binds nothing, array lengths stay unbound and read). Fixture expects sized->N; mutant go/arraylen-param-shadow CAUGHT.

decisions.node_type: map-literal key reads
decisions.question: Go second review (2026-09-13): every keyed-element first child was treated as a struct key, so map-literal keys (`map[Color]int{Red: 1}`) stayed silent though key expressions genuinely read (probe-verified missing pair; the old comment claimed the shapes were identical).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: the enclosing composite literal's type decides — map_type literals read their keys, everything else (struct/slice/elided) keeps the old silence. Fixture expects keyed->Red; mutant go/map-key-silence CAUGHT.

decisions.node_type: builtin-receiver call filter
decisions.question: Go second review (2026-09-13): the builtin guard matched the RECEIVER segment, dropping every qualified call on a builtin-named package (`copy.DeepCopyValue` from terraform/internal/copy never emitted — terraform rotation MISSING; every other call site already used leaf semantics, including the oracle).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: isGoBuiltin matches the callee leaf (identical behavior at all leaf-passing sites; preserves the deliberate `v.len()` rule). Fixture expects calls duplicate->DeepCopyValue; mutant go/builtin-receiver-drop CAUGHT. Lane rot-2 clean after.

decisions.node_type: generic type-parameter binding
decisions.question: Go second review (2026-09-13): generic type parameters never bound (the entry loop visited parameter_list only, though params parse as parameter_declaration under type_parameter_list too), so a colliding file value misattributed on invalid code (`return T` emitted f->T for the const).
decisions.resolution: FIXED, explicitly unpinned: no valid-Go observable exists (a value-position use of a type-param name does not compile; type positions never read), so no fixture/mutant covers it — the shared bindParamsOf path is fixture-pinned via GO10, and lanes + F3 confirm zero valid-code impact. Kept for robustness on error-tolerant parses (3 lines).

decisions.node_type: grammar ERROR regions (composite literal, call/selector chains)
decisions.question: The pinned tree-sitter-go errors on two LEGAL constructs — a package-scope generic function VALUE (`var _ = slices.Backward[[]int]`, Go 1.21+) and a method on an INSTANTIATED GENERIC RECEIVER (`func (Either[A, B]) A() A`, Go 1.18+) — and its error RECOVERY re-reads the FOLLOWING declaration's text as a composite literal (`func caller(s []int) {` -> `composite_literal "s []int) { _ = s }"`). Both sides derived `instantiates -> s` from it: a construction of a name the source never constructs, named after a PARAMETER.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PINNED (#799 round): a grammar error region is not evidence of a construction. The analyzer's composite-literal pass skips ERROR/isMissing subtrees, and the oracle's `composite_literal` branch refuses to read a literal inside one — while STILL DESCENDING, because real declarations sit deeper inside recovered regions (the `!leaf` prune of GO16 is the second half of that rule). Blast radius measured from the tree's own ERROR regions, not from a line count: 20 of 1,931 go-tools files parse with an error and 3 of them swallow declarations (92 in total, 37 from the generic-value shape: slicesbackward.go 37, slicescontains.go 31, internal/gcimporter/testdata/genmeth/a.go 24); terraform 0 of 1,993. 15 fabricated rows removed on go-tools. Fixture go/grammar-error-not-a-construction-889 (forbidRelationships names the fabricated edge) + mutant go/error-region-construction CAUGHT.

decisions.node_type: package-scope call walk (callee that cannot be NAMED)
decisions.question: `analyzeGoPackageScopeCalls` returned on any call_expression whose callee it could not name (parenthesized, index/generic instantiation, or parse-recovery debris), abandoning the node's whole SUBTREE. Measured at full extent: the only two non-implements MISSING rows the lane had were `s[i].Lock()` / `s[i].Unlock()` in go-tools/go/analysis/passes/modernize/testdata/src/slicesbackward/slicesbackward.go — lost while `s[i].String()`, twelve lines later in the SAME recovery region, was emitted. The difference was recovery luck, not source.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PINNED (#799 round): an unnameable callee claims no edge (it names no target) but the walk DESCENDS, exactly like the oracle's flat DFS. Full extent: MISSING 12 -> 10, analyzer edges +2, unexplained unchanged (2, both the #914 implements class). Fixture go/error-region-callee-descend-799 (expects calls -> Lock and calls -> Unlock; also pins `Backward[[]int](tail(nil))` -> calls -> tail, the generic-callee form of the same rule) + mutant go/error-region-callee-prunes-subtree CAUGHT.

decisions.node_type: qualified type USE (references/declared_type, references/return_type)
decisions.question: A qualified type use was published as SOURCE TEXT — `io.Reader`, `testing.T`, `types.Importer`, `template.Template` (1,162 + 56 rows on a 400-file draw) — while the lane's own `uses` targeted selector LEAVES (`pkg.Fn` -> `Fn`) and struct/interface embedding's `extends` had just been moved to the leaf. One node kind, two answers; and `.` is a character no Go declaration may contain, which is how `references|.` entered the lane's R10 separator vocabulary.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PINNED (#799 round, R10): a qualified type use is published under the LEAF the lane would declare for that type (`Reader`, `T`, `Importer`, `Template`) with the package-qualified spelling kept in `metadata.qualifiedType`. Fixtures go/type-usage-graph + go/relationship-and-payloads pin leaf + metadata; mutant go/qualified-type-raw-text CAUGHT by both. Separator targets 39,280 -> 11,933 over the full draw.

decisions.node_type: import dependency (the import_spec edge)
decisions.question: The dependency edge carried the `references` label with the module SPECIFIER as its target (`net/http`, `github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp`), which put `/`, `.` and `-` into the references TARGET surface — a vocabulary that could only be excused by an R10 ruling which would then also excuse a real spelling defect on the same label. A module specifier is not a name: it is a string literal naming a module.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PINNED (#799 round, R10): the dependency now rides the family's FIRST-CLASS `imports` kind (the direction #910 took for c; go's own requiredKinds has named `imports` since the systems wave), with `metadata.isImport` + `isGoImportDep` KEPT — completeness section B pins the kind from the marker, and classifyEvidenceTier gained the `imports` -> import_based branch (the seam the kotlin/T1 regression class lives in). The references surface is now separator-free, so a future foreign spelling there fails R10 immediately. Fixtures go/relationship-and-payloads (imports -> fmt) + go/callsite-lines-825 (the import_spec's line) + mutant go/import-dep-labeled-reference CAUGHT.

decisions.node_type: struct embedding of an INSTANTIATED GENERIC (extends, oracle side)
decisions.question: An embedded field that instantiates a generic (`listers.ResourceIndexer[*crv1.Example]`, `*gentype.ClientWithListAndApply[*crv1.Example, *crv1.ExampleList, *applyconfigurationcrv1.ExampleApplyConfiguration]` — kubernetes' generated client code is built out of these) was named by the ORACLE as `lastSegment(raw text)`, whose last dot lands INSIDE the type arguments: it published `Example]` and `CustomResourceDefinitionApplyConfiguration]` as the embedded type's NAME. The analyzer, fixed in this round's #889 work, publishes the LEAF of the base type (`ResourceIndexer`, `ClientWithListAndApply`) — which is what Go promotes. The two sides then disagreed in bulk, and the disagreement was invisible on BOTH pinned corpora, which carry zero generic embedded fields.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PINNED (round 3, the go-heavy corpus read): the oracle resolves an embedded field's name through `goEmbeddedLeaf` (differential.ts) — unwrap pointer_type/generic_type, take the leaf after the last `.`, validate it as an identifier — mirrored in BOTH oracle places that resolve an embedding (`deriveGoEdges`' extends and `deriveGoImplements`' struct-embedding promotion map, where the pre-fix leaf had also fabricated a promotion from a TYPE ARGUMENT and omitted the real embedded type). Measured on kubernetes @90777f0b (13,488 non-vendor `.go` files, read in chunks): #648 MISSING + 557 UNEXPLAINED `extends` rows -> MISSING 12+54+24 = 90, UNEXPLAINED 0, every remaining row the #914 `implements` class. Unmoved where the shape does not occur: go-tools full extent 1,931 files / truth 30,700 / MISSING 10 / unexplained 2 and terraform 1,993 / 40,927 / 22 / 0 — byte-identical before and after, and the pinned F5 draw (`--repo terraform --sample 60`) still reads 1,228/1,228 with unexplained 0. PIN: `F9-PROBE-GO-EMBED-GENERIC` in script/m14/verify-probe-battery.ts asserts the leaf on BOTH sides and forbids the bracket text with `oracleForbid`; executed negative — with the oracle reverted the battery reads `FAIL … oracle no longer derives: extends:exampleLister->ResourceIndexer, extends:examples->ClientWithListAndApply (oracle regression)` and blocks release.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: Both pinned corpora carry ZERO generic embedded fields and the canonical F5 gates read DRAWS of them, so no draw could ever contain the shape; and an oracle defect cannot be pinned by a fixture, because fixtures compare the analyzer against an expectation, never the truth against the tree. The class was found by reading a corpus 4.5x their size at full extent (reviews/go/fourth-review.md).

decisions.node_type: variadic_parameter_declaration in an INTERFACE method_spec; the parameter payload's isVariadic flag; the implements signature compare
decisions.question: `extractGoMethodSpecParameters` accepted only `parameter_declaration`, so EVERY variadic interface method lost its last parameter: `Logf(format string, args ...any)` on the DECLARED side became `Logf(string) void` while the implementor kept `args` as a real parameter, and `buildGoMethodSignature` then compared two different signatures — the pair was silently un-satisfiable. That is not an edge case in Go: every grpc-generated client method ends in `opts ...grpc.CallOption`, and terraform's view interfaces are `Output(code InitMessageCode, args ...any)`. It also FABRICATED: `unimplementedDialer.Dial(ctx, addr)` matched `Dialer.Dial(ctx, addr string, opts ...string)` once the declared side had lost `opts`, so the analyzer declared a fixed-arity server type to implement a variadic client interface Go refuses. Separately, the parameter's `...` marker was dropped in the payload by BOTH extractors (`typeNode?.text` is the ELEMENT type), so `H(x ...string)` and `H(x string)` produced the same canonical signature.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PINNED (round 4): `extractGoMethodSpecParameters` reads the same node set as `extractGoParameters` — `parameter_declaration` OR `variadic_parameter_declaration` — and both extractors publish `isVariadic: true` on a variadic parameter (the family convention: python/lua do the same; the payload's `type` stays the ELEMENT type, so no existing pin or consumer changes meaning). `buildGoMethodSignature` renders `...` in front of such a parameter, and `normalizeGoSignature` keeps it (`...T` is a DIFFERENT Go type from `T` and from `[]T`). The oracle derives the identical text from the tree (`goSignatureParameterTypes`), so the compare is a comparison of signatures on both sides. Measured: go-tools full extent 1,931 files MISSING 10 -> 0, terraform 1,993 files MISSING 22 -> 0, kubernetes 13,488 files MISSING 90 -> 0. PIN: fixture go/implements-signature-914 (expectParameters name `isVariadic` on the field, forbidParameters name the collapsed spellings) + `F9-PROBE-GO-IMPL-SIGNATURE`; the F3 parameters matcher now enforces EVERY key a pin names, not just name/type, because an unpinnable payload field is exactly where a regression hides. FOUR mutants: go/impl-iface-variadic-param-dropped, go/impl-variadic-marker-stripped (plus the two below) — all CAUGHT.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: The canonical F5 draw reads 60 files per lane and neither pinned corpus is grpc-heavy: the shape needs an interface method whose LAST parameter is variadic AND an implementor in the SAME file. It survives a fixture suite too, because every existing implements fixture used non-variadic methods — the pre-fix analyzer's own fixture (go/implements-params) passes both before and after, and go-tools' 10 MISSING rows were 2 files out of 1,931. The fabrication half is the C5 collusion pattern in its purest form: the ORACLE compared method NAMES only, so it derived `unimplementedDialer -> Dialer` as well, the differential agreed, and a wrong contract reported 0 unexplained.

decisions.node_type: implements implementor candidates (method receiver type names) vs declared type symbols
decisions.question: The candidates were the types DECLARED in the file (`kind === Struct || Type`), but a Go method set is a PACKAGE-level property. gopls declares `clientDispatcher` in gopls/internal/protocol/protocol.go and all 21 of `Client`'s methods in tsclient.go, so the file holds every method the interface needs and no declaration of the implementor — the analyzer emitted NOTHING for a pair it could prove, and the oracle (which has always keyed its implementor map by receiver NAME) emitted it. On go-tools that was 2 rows (tsclient.go, tsserver.go) and on terraform 2 more (internal/collections/cmp.go: Map/Set -> transformerForCmp, whose types are generic instantiations declared elsewhere).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PINNED (round 4): the candidate list is declared non-interface types PLUS every receiver type name with no same-file declaration (`analyzeGoInterfaceImplementation`). Mirrored exactly on both sides — a name with no declaration cannot be a declared generic, so no generics skip applies, and a type whose embedding is declared elsewhere cannot promote, so neither side invents promotion. Measured: go-tools 193 implements truth edges, terraform 295, both sides identical at full extent, 0 MISSING / 0 UNEXPLAINED. PIN: fixture go/implements-signature-914 expects `implements clientDispatcher -> Client` where the type is declared NOWHERE in the file (deliberately); mutant go/impl-receiver-only-candidate-dropped reconstructs the pre-fix reading (an implements source that is not a declared type symbol) and is CAUGHT.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: Both rows live in ONE file each, and the F5 draw samples 60 of 1,931 files: tsclient.go was never drawn. The oracle already emitted both edges, so at the differential's 60-file resolution the lane read 0/0 either way; only a FULL-EXTENT read (script/m14/tmp/go-799-surface.ts) could see them, and the pinned F5 floor cannot. It is also the asymmetry class the corpus cannot police — when the truth already knows something the analyzer does not, a draw that misses the file reports perfect agreement.

decisions.node_type: type_alias with an interface_type (and a struct_type) — `type A = interface{ M() }`
decisions.question: The ORACLE registered interfaces from `type_spec` nodes only (`if (!ts || ts.type !== "type_spec") continue`), but a type ALIAS parses as `type_alias`. So `type A = interface{ M() }` never entered the oracle's `interfaces` map, and `type T interface { A }` — whose embedded element folds A's method set — folded NOTHING. go-tools internal/gcimporter/testdata/issue25301.go was the lane's ONLY unexplained pair at full extent, both rows this one shape (`S -> A`, `S -> T`): the analyzer emitted two correct implements edges the truth could not explain. The alias node declares the same `name` and `type` fields as the spec, so it is read through the identical path; the analyzer had already published `interface:A` and `interface:A@T` (its own alias handling was right).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PINNED (round 4): `deriveGoImplements` accepts `type_spec` OR `type_alias` for the interface, struct-embedding and generics bookkeeping. Measured: go-tools unexplained 2 -> 0 at full extent (1,931 files), and the alias case is pinned BOTH ways — fixture go/implements-signature-914 expects `implements AliasImpl -> Alias` and `implements AliasImpl -> Embedder` (the interface that embeds the alias), and `F9-PROBE-GO-IMPL-SIGNATURE` asserts the same two edges with `oracleForbid`. Executed negative: with HEAD's oracle the probe reads `oracle no longer derives: implements:AliasImpl->Alias, implements:AliasImpl->Embedder (oracle regression)` — it is the expect-side oracle check that fires first.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: An alias-to-interface is rare in real code (1 file in 1,931 on go-tools, 0 on terraform and 0 in the kubernetes chunks) and the differential only reports it as UNEXPLAINED when the analyzer's own reading is right — a lane that had ALSO skipped the alias would have reported 0/0 while both sides were blind.

decisions.node_type: embedded-interface method folding, DIAMOND shape (`A { B; C }`, `B { D }`, `C { D }`)
decisions.question: Both sides marked an interface visited and never released the mark, so it was a GLOBAL seen set rather than a path mark: the first branch to reach D consumed it and the second branch's lookup returned nothing. For `A { B; C }` with `B { D }` and `C { D }` that left C (and A) without D's methods by declaration order alone. The analyzer's `getGoInterfaceMethods` threaded one shared `seen` set through the recursion; the oracle's `fold` copied `interfaces[e]` BEFORE folding `e`, so a two-hop embedding only ever contributed through whichever of the pair happened to be visited second. Each side lost it in a DIFFERENT shape, which is why the differential reported perfect agreement on a contract both sides had wrong.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PINNED (round 4): the analyzer releases its visiting mark on the way out (a path mark; the entry check still carries the G12 `A { B }; B { A }` cycle guard); the oracle resolves the embedded interface FULLY first and then merges, on both the interface and the struct-promotion folds. PINNED by `F9-PROBE-GO-IMPL-SIGNATURE`, which expects `Diamond -> D/B/C/A` and forbids nothing else: pre-fix the ORACLE derived only D/B/C (losing `Diamond->A`) while the ANALYZER kept A but dropped the forbidden set, so the probe's expect-plus-forbid pair is what makes the shape visible. Executed negative against HEAD's code: 5 of 8 expected edges missing and 5 forbidden edges fabricated; post-fix 8/8 and 0.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: A diamond needs three interface declarations and an implementor in one file, and it needs the two sides to lose the edge in different ways before the differential can charge anyone. The corpora's embeddings are 1-deep, so the shape never occurred; and where only ONE side lost it, the row would have been a single MISSING in a 1,931-file read with a 50-row sample cap — invisible at the F5 floor either way.

decisions.node_type: implements truth derivation (oracle): method NAME set vs canonical method SIGNATURE
decisions.question: The oracle compared method NAME sets only, documented as a deliberate simplification (`name-set equality is the sufficient, stable truth`). It is a strict SUPERSET of Go's satisfaction rule, so it published pairs Go REFUSES and charged every one of them to the analyzer as a MISSING edge that could never be closed: go-tools `Value -> Type` (`Elem() Value` against `Elem() Type` — go/ssa/interp/testdata/src/reflect/reflect.go), `VS/VT/mybool/T -> VI` and `VS/VT/mybool -> I` (go/ssa/interp/testdata/coverage.go, where `VT.f(x int, y ...string)` was declared to satisfy `VI.f(x int)`); terraform `InitJSON/InitHuman -> Init` and `StateMigrateHuman -> StateMigrate` (`Output(code InitMessageCode, args ...any)`), `Diff -> DiffRenderer`, `ReferenceMap -> GraphNodeReferencer`, `graphTransformerMulti -> GraphVertexTransformer`, and every `UnimplementedXServer -> XClient` in the grpc generated code.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PINNED (round 4): `deriveGoImplements` compares the analyzer's canonical signature text, derived independently from the tree in the oracle (`goSignatureText` + `normalizeGoSignatureText`: parameters by TYPE only, grouped declarations expanded one parameter per name, a variadic parameter rendered `...T`, named results reduced to their types, no result = `void`, whitespace collapsed and `interface{}` -> `any`). Implementor candidates are receiver type names (GO21) and each pair is compared method-by-method. Measured: go-tools truth 193 implements edges with 0 MISSING and 0 UNEXPLAINED at full extent, terraform 295 / 0 / 0, kubernetes 0/0 over 13,488 files in four index-range chunks with 0 parse skips. PIN: `F9-PROBE-GO-IMPL-SIGNATURE`'s forbid list (StrictType/Elem-return, ArityIface/arity, SliceIface/`[]T`-vs-`...T`, Dialer/variadic, BareIface/`T`-vs-`...T`) with `oracleForbid`, so the truth must refuse all five. Executed negative against HEAD's code: the pre-fix oracle fabricated all five; post-fix it fabricates none and derives all 8 expected edges, and the pre-fix ANALYZER fabricated two of them (`unimplementedDialer -> Dialer`, `VariadicOnly -> BareIface`) which the probe now forbids. Fixture go/implements-signature-914 pins the same five absences on the analyzer side.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: A name-only truth can only be caught by a pair whose names match and whose signatures do not, and every such row is reported as MISSING — i.e. as an ANALYZER defect. The lane carried 9 go-tools + 18 terraform + 90 kubernetes 'missing implements' rows for four rounds, and the majority were the TRUTH being wrong; the F5 floor reads the same rows as 0/0 because a 60-file draw almost never contains a same-file name-collision pair. The simplification was documented in the oracle's own comment, which is exactly why no gate could see it: the comment asserted the analyzer 'also satisfies' a superset check, and it does not.

decisions.node_type: method_spec as a package-scope callable (bare-call resolution)
decisions.question: A `method_spec` is published as `kind: Method`, and the declared-callable set accepted any Function/Method by NAME. So a name that exists in the file ONLY as an interface method resolved as a bare callee and published `calls` edges (`global -> Handle`, `g -> Handle`). The F5 oracle's `declaredFns` is built from `function_declaration` + `method_declaration` only, so the truth could not derive them: the differential read them as UNEXPLAINED, the fabrication class. It is a C5 asymmetry — the mirror image of #914 — and NEITHER pinned corpus contains the shape (a file that declares an interface method and calls that name bare is not legal Go, so neither corpus has one).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PROBE-PINNED. `isGoPackageCallable` is the single predicate at all three call-resolution sites (resolveGoFunctionCall, the package-scope pass's `declared` set, isGoResolvableCallTarget) and refuses `metadata.isInterfaceMethod`. A bare callee resolves to a DECLARED function or method, which is what Go's scope rules say and what the oracle already modelled.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: F4 runs FIXTURES, and F3 pins what a fixture can express; the shape needs a file the compiler rejects, so no valid-Go fixture reaches it (the same situation GO14 recorded). The pin is `F9-PROBE-GO-BARE-CALLABLE-SET`, which carries `oracleForbid` so a future lockstep that mirrored the wrong rule would fail rather than agree. NO MUTANT: one was written (`go/iface-method-name-as-callee`) and PROVEN to survive, because the defect is not observable from any valid-Go emission; it was removed rather than left in the set as decoration. The probe was proven able to fail by executing the revert (it reports `fabricated: calls:Handle`).

decisions.node_type: implements self-pair (analyzer side)
decisions.question: The oracle has always carried `if (structName === iface) continue`; the analyzer had no such guard, so a tree carrying two declarations of the same name — invalid Go, which tree-sitter-go accepts and error recovery produces — published `implements I -> I` while the truth refused the pair. A rule present on one side of a compared label only is a fabrication by the family's definition, and this is the class round 4 named when it added the guard to the oracle.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PROBE-PINNED. The guard is added to the candidate loop, so both sides carry it.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: Same as GO25: no valid-Go file can declare a type and an interface with one name. The mutant `go/impl-self-pair-emitted` was written and PROVEN to survive for the same reason and removed; the pin is `F9-PROBE-GO-BARE-CALLABLE-SET` (forbid `implements:H->H`), proven able to fail by executing the revert.

decisions.node_type: isGoExported (ASCII range) vs the spec's Unicode upper-case rule
decisions.question: Go's spec: an identifier is exported if its first character is a UNICODE upper case letter. The test was `name[0] >= "A" && name[0] <= "Z"`, so every legal Go identifier with a non-ASCII head (`Ünï`, `Ö`, `Ä`) was published `visibility: "private"` — and `private` fails the PHASE-5 export predicate, so the symbol was dropped from the public-API export list the product serves entirely. This is not a classification nicety: a whole file's public API can vanish from the index.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + FIXTURE-PINNED. The test is now a no-regex upper-case test on the first CODE POINT using the runtime's own Unicode case mappings: `c` is an upper-case letter exactly when `toUpperCase(c) === c && toLowerCase(c) !== c`, which is `unicode.IsUpper`'s definition (the Go spec words the category test as "the uppercase version of the letter is different from its lowercase version"). Spot-checked against the categories that matter: `A` upper, `a` not, `Ü` upper, `ü` not, `ß` not (Ll), CJK not (Lo), titlecase `ǅ` not (Lt). The residual — a code point the runtime's tables do not know — resolves to NOT-exported, the conservative direction. Fixture `go/round5-surfaces` + mutant `go/export-ascii-only`.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round5-verify.ts case F1/F2 with control F3

decisions.node_type: predeclared identifier set (missing `comparable`)
decisions.question: Go's PREDECLARED identifiers include `comparable` (the generics-era type-constraint interface) alongside `any` and `error`. The declared-type exclusion set held `any` and `error` but not `comparable` — the set predates generics. Because the pinned grammar types a generic type-parameter list as `parameter_declaration` nodes, `type Pair[K comparable, V any]` reached the `parameter_declaration` case and published a `declared_type` target `Pair -> comparable`, a name no declaration in any file can define. The presence of `any` and the absence of `comparable` in the same set is the tell.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + FIXTURE-PINNED. `comparable` joins the set. Fixture `go/round5-surfaces` (forbid `declared_type -> comparable`; forbid a `comparable` member owned by `Pair`) + mutant `go/predeclared-comparable-leaks`.
decisions.why_not_the_constraint_elem_surface: `type T interface{ comparable }` still publishes the member and the `extends` edge, and that is RULED CORRECT rather than fixed: `comparable` is a predeclared INTERFACE type, so embedding it is real composition under exactly the same rule that publishes `io.Closer` as a member leaf. Only the DECLARED-TYPE reference was wrong, because a predeclared name is not a declared type in this file. Pinned as a control in the same fixture so the ruling cannot be quietly reversed.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round5-verify.ts case E1 with controls E2/E3

decisions.node_type: parameter_declaration labelled by arity instead of by the `result` field
decisions.question: `emit(resolveSource(n), [n], n.namedChildCount === 1 ? "return_type" : "declared_type")` — a SHAPE heuristic. An unnamed PARAMETER (`func f(*Server, Server)`) and an unnamed RESULT (`func h() (*S, error)`) are both one-named-child `parameter_declaration` nodes, so every unnamed parameter was published as a `return_type` reference. Nothing in the predicate looked at which list the declaration is in, and the tree says: the result list is the `result` FIELD of the enclosing function/method/method_spec/func_literal (probe-verified on all four).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + FIXTURE-PINNED. `isGoResultParameter` reads the field, and `variadic_parameter_declaration` is now handled by the same case (it was not, so a variadic parameter's type never reached the declared-type graph). Fixture `go/round5-surfaces` pins `takesUnnamed -> Server` as `declared_type`, forbids the `return_type` spelling, and pins `returnsUnnamed -> Server` as `return_type` and `namedParam -> Server` as `declared_type` as controls; mutant `go/unnamed-param-as-return-type` reconstructs the pre-fix labelling from the payload's own `arg<N>` parameter-name signature.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round5-verify.ts case D1 with controls D2/D3

decisions.node_type: Module symbol range (hand-built literal) and var/const symbol range (declaration, not name)
decisions.question: Two range defects with one shape: a range computed from something other than the node the symbol is written on. (a) The package Module's range was a hand-built literal — `startLine: 1, startColumn: 1, startIndex: 0, endIndex: name.length + 8` — which is only right when the package clause is the first thing in the file, and a `//go:build` header sits above it in 158 of the two pinned corpora's 3,924 files and 2,462 of kubernetes's 17,848. Every byte of the range pointed into the build-tag comment. (b) A var/const symbol took the whole `var_spec` range while the struct-field path deliberately took the NAME node's range and documents why (#919: `A, B int` names two fields at two positions, and a consumer that jumps to `B` must land on `B`); so on `var alpha,\n\tBeta int` both names reported the first name's position and `Beta`'s own position appeared nowhere in the index.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + FIXTURE-PINNED. (a) the range is `nodeToRange(packageClause)`, read from the node — which makes GO4's finding structural rather than arithmetic and is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the old literal for a clause at byte 0 (`endIndex: len+8`, `endColumn: len+9`), so the common case's output does not move. (b) the range is `nodeToRange(nameNode)`. Fixture `go/round5-surfaces` carries a `//go:build` header (which is what makes (a) reachable) and pins both `alpha`/`Beta` and the grouped const `Gone`/`AlsoGo`; mutants `go/module-range-hardcoded` and `go/var-name-uses-decl-range`.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: No existing fixture had a `//go:build` header, and no existing fixture asserted a var/const range at all. (b) has NO MUTANT: one was written and PROVEN to survive, because the pre-fix range came from the `var_spec` NODE and no symbol payload field identifies that node — the defect is not reconstructible from the emitted output at all. The fixture's `expectSymbolRanges` rows are the pin, and they were proven able to fail by executing the revert (11 range assertions went red).

decisions.node_type: alias-to-struct embedding, and the `SymbolKind.Class` predicates
decisions.question: Two dead-logic classes with the same root cause — a predicate naming something the analyzer never produces. (a) `type A = struct{ *Inner }` is legal Go; the SYMBOL path accepted `type_spec || type_alias` but the EMBEDDING pass read `type_spec` only (as did the F5 oracle, so the two agreed on the omission and no differential could charge it), so the member symbol was published and the `extends` edge was not: the graph claimed `A` contains `Inner` while `A` extended nothing. (b) Five predicates tested `s.kind === SymbolKind.Class`, and the go analyzer has NEVER emitted a Class symbol (Go's struct is `SymbolKind.Struct`), so every one was vacuously FALSE. Two of them are product features that have therefore never once fired: `generateGoArchitecturalInsights`' `struct_design` insight (struct count, method:struct ratio, the anemic/balanced/rich verdict) was never emitted for any Go file, and `calculateArchitecturalScore`'s +3 struct-design bonus could never be granted. A third was `getGoFrameworkPatterns`' `case "gorm"`, unreachable for a third reason: the file-level and per-import framework detectors were two INDEPENDENTLY WRITTEN vocabularies that disagreed in both directions, so `gorm` was known to one and could never be pushed into the other.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + FIXTURE-PINNED. (a) the embedding pass accepts `type_alias` and the ORACLE was changed in the same round (both sides, C5 discipline — a one-sided fix would have turned a shared omission into a fabrication). (b) the predicates name `SymbolKind.Struct`, and the two framework readers now resolve through ONE table (`GO_FRAMEWORK_RULES`) so the vocabularies cannot drift again. Fixture `go/round5-surfaces` pins `extends Alias -> Inner`, pins `architecturalScore` at the value that INCLUDES the +3 bonus (the fixture carries methods on `Inner` specifically to bring its ratio inside the [1,5] band the bonus needs, so a vacuous struct list moves the pin by exactly the bonus), and pins the gorm detection. Mutants `go/alias-struct-embedding-dropped`, `go/struct-kind-class-vacuous`, `go/framework-vocab-drift`.
decisions.ruling_on_golang_extended: `golang.org/x/...` is a CATEGORY (a namespace), not a framework, and the table marks it `listed: false` so it stays a per-import marker and never enters `detectedFrameworks` — promoting it would make almost every modern Go file report a framework. That is a deliberate exclusion recorded here rather than left to a reader.

decisions.node_type: declared-type reference graph: per-(source,target,relType) dedupe vs per-site edges
decisions.question: `extractDeclaredTypeRefs` dedupes file-globally on `(source, target, relType)`, so the 2nd..Nth SITE of the same type in the same owner is dropped and only the FIRST site's line survives. A struct with three `*TypeGraph` fields publishes ONE edge, at the first field's line. LANE-AUDIT-FORMULA §8 asks for relationships to carry the site line "per-site not per-set".
decisions.ruling: RULED AS THE LANE'S CONVENTION, NOT FIXED. The lane already carries the per-set-with-first-site rule as a pinned family contract for the other payload-shaped surface: `qualified_calls` is a UNIQUE set of callee paths per function symbol (GOD9, rust #383) and `analyzeGoFunctionCalls` emits ONE `calls` edge per (source, target) with the first site's line, pinned by the mutant `go/duplicate-qualified-calls` (which reverted the dedupe and was caught). `declared_type` follows the same rule, so the two surfaces answer the same question the same way. Changing it would multiply `references/declared_type` edges by roughly the mean fields-per-declaration (15,598 on etcd, 18,422 on grpc-go) to add line numbers the M59.A7 line oracle never reads — it only checks the `calls` label. HONEST GAP, DISCLOSED: (i) the `references` label carries no line at all under the per-set reading of §8, and the line oracle does not cover it, so this surface is unmeasured by the lane's line gate; (ii) the surviving edge's `metadata.qualifiedType` is order-dependent, so which spelling is kept for a repeated type depends on declaration order. Neither is a wrong edge; both are named rather than left to be discovered.

decisions.node_type: contains pass: a member whose name equals its owner
decisions.question: The contains pass reads `if (owner && owner !== s.name)`, so a legal same-named member (`type Foo struct { Foo string }`, `type T interface{ T() int }`) is PUBLISHED as a symbol and its `contains Foo -> Foo` edge is NOT emitted. The graph can name the member but cannot answer "what is inside Foo" completely.
decisions.ruling: RULED, GUARD KEPT. The guard's intent is to refuse a self-loop, and a self-loop in a membership surface is a hazard for every consumer that traverses `contains` (it is an infinite path in a naive walk, and `contains` is the surface a call-graph or dependency-graph builder walks first). The member is still published, and its `extends`/`implements` relationships still name it, so it is reachable; what it loses is one membership row. The alternative — publishing the self-loop — would push the hazard into the graph to preserve a completeness figure. This is a language-construct judgement, and the lane records the judgement rather than the figure.

decisions.node_type: implements pass complexity (promoted-method closure + signature re-derivation)
decisions.question: `collectGoPromotedMethods` was called INSIDE the candidate loop, which is inside the interface loop, even though a candidate's promoted-method set depends on the candidate ALONE. Inside it, the whole method list was re-filtered at every embedding hop and every method signature was re-derived on every comparison, with no memoization. Measured on synthetic files: 80 interfaces x 80 structs with embedding cost 17.4 s, and ms/KB climbed 35 -> 64 -> 361 -> 662 as the file doubled. LANE-AUDIT-FORMULA §9 asks for a scaling check per size band precisely so that a flat ms/KB is required; this was not flat.
decisions.resolution: FIXED. The closure is computed once per candidate into a map before the interface loop, and `buildGoMethodSignature` is memoized per method node (`goSignatures`, keyed by the file-local `startIndex` and reset in `analyze()` beside `goCallSites` for the same reason). The emitted edge SET is unchanged — the fixture `go/implements-signature-914` and the promoted-implements mutant `go/drop-promoted-struct-implements` both still hold, which is the point: this is a cost fix with no behavioural delta, so it cannot be mutant-pinned and is measured instead.

decisions.node_type: name-keyed plain objects (`{}`) vs Go identifiers that shadow Object.prototype
decisions.question: Four maps in the analyzer are keyed by a Go NAME and were plain object literals: the struct-embedding map `embeddedOf`, the framework/insight dedupe `seen`, and `parseStructTags`'s result. Go identifiers may be any Unicode letter followed by letters and digits, so a legal type may be named `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, `__proto__` and the rest of Object.prototype — `embeddedOf['constructor']` then returns the Object constructor (truthy, not an array) and the embedding write `.push` throws. The F5 ORACLE already builds all five of its own name-keyed maps with `Object.create(null)`, with a comment recording that a legal Go type named constructor/toString/valueOf once made the lane CRASH OUTRIGHT on go-tools/go/callgraph/vta/vta.go. The analyzer never got the same defence. The defect stayed latent only because `collectGoPromotedMethods` used to be reached for fewer candidates; the GO34 hoist removed that accidental restriction and the FULL-EXTENT go-tools read crashed on vta.go — the exact file the oracle names.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + PROBE-PINNED. All four maps are `Object.create(null)`. The pin is `script/m14/tmp/go-round5-proto-names.ts` (eight prototype names, each a struct that embeds, has methods, is aliased, and carries a struct tag whose key is the same name), run against BOTH analyzers: pre-fix throws on all 8, post-fix publishes all 8 and derives the implements edges. A crash cannot be fixture-pinned, so the probe is the pin.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: The 1,931-file go-tools FULL-EXTENT read is a probe, not a gate — the F5 canonical draw is 60 files and the fixtures are 13. A prototype-named type is rare enough that a 60-file draw can miss it even though go-tools carries one at go/callgraph/vta/vta.go. FOUND BY THE READ, on the corpus the read exists for.

decisions.node_type: declared-type source attribution: a type ALIAS is a type declaration
decisions.question: `resolveSource` attributed a field's declared type to the nearest enclosing `type_spec`. `type_alias` is a type declaration too — it DECLARES the name (`type Alias = struct{ Q Inner }` declares `Alias`) — so an alias's field types found no enclosing declaration, fell through the whole ancestor chain, and were attributed to `global`. `global` is a pseudo-source: it names no declaration, so the edge was unattributable and no consumer could navigate back to the declaration that wanted the type. Contrast: `type Plain struct{ Q Inner }` correctly gave `Plain -> Inner`. This is the SECOND HALF of GO31a, which taught the embedding pass to accept `type_alias` and left the declared-type resolver behind — a half-fix that read as done because the `extends` edge it did cover was correct.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + FIXTURE-PINNED + MUTANT. `resolveSource` accepts `type_spec || type_alias`; the round-6 truth's R3 rule states the same. Fixture `go/round5-surfaces` expects `references Alias -> Holder` and forbids the `global` spelling for both alias-owned targets; mutant `go/alias-field-type-to-global` reconstructs the pre-fix re-sourcing from the output (an alias struct that owns members).
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: TWO independent reasons, and the second is the important one. (1) `references` was EXCLUDED from go's compared-label set, so no differential could see it at all — 127,061 edges outside the comparison. (2) Even after the round-6 truth went into the allowlist, the harness matcher compares `label + normTarget(target)` and IGNORES the edge's source (script/m14/differential.ts:15634), so a source-attribution defect is structurally invisible to F5. On go-tools the class is 16 rows over 1,931 files — 0.07% — and go-tools carries only 10 files with `type X = struct`, so a 60-file draw has roughly a 1-in-3 chance of touching one and the fixture set had none. The class is therefore pinned by FIXTURE and MUTANT, and the full-triple comparison lives in the round-6 probe (`go-round6-references-corpus.ts`), which matches on (source, target, relationshipType) rather than label+target. THAT MATCHER LIMITATION IS A DISCLOSED LIMITATION, not a defect: no go `references` edge's SOURCE is differential-audited.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round6-references-shapes.ts case S10; script/m14/tmp/go-round6-references-corpus.ts (16 MISSING + 16 UNEXPLAINED with the fix reverted, 0/0 with it); reviews/go/sixth-review.md

decisions.node_type: a `function_type`'s internal result list vs a declared function's `result` field
decisions.question: `return_type` vs `declared_type` is decided by whether the declaration sits in a `result` list. Both the analyzer and the round-6 truth originally accepted `function_type` as a result-bearing owner, so a field whose type is a function type — `Fn func(a A, b B) (A, error)` — produced a `return_type` reference from the field. The disagreement was the FIRST one the two derivations produced that was not a defect in either, which made it worth a semantic argument rather than a fix.
decisions.ruling: RULED: a `parameter_declaration` inside a `function_type` is part of a TYPE EXPRESSION and does NOT produce a separate `return_type`; the enclosing declaration's type expression yields one `declared_type`. The distinction is Go's own: a `parameter_declaration` in a `function_declaration`'s `result` FIELD is the declaration of THAT function's result, and the grammar gives the list its own field precisely so it can be told apart; a `parameter_declaration` inside a function TYPE describes that type, not anything the file declares. Labelling it `return_type` would claim a struct returns a type, and it carries no information the `declared_type` edge does not — same source, same target, and the product's `references` edge is name-only, so nothing can consume the distinction. The round-6 truth carries the same exclusion, and S11/S14 pin the ruling as CONTROLS so it cannot be quietly reversed.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round6-references-shapes.ts cases S11 and S14

decisions.node_type: type_spec / type_alias inside a function body
decisions.question: `extractGoSymbols` `continue`d on every function_declaration and method_declaration, so the walk never reached a `type` declaration written inside a function body — the type, its field symbols and its `contains` edges were all absent. Go permits local type declarations and both pinned corpora use them as a matter of course (go-tools declares 22 local-type memberships in its first 200 files). The silence was NOT NEUTRAL, which is what makes this a defect rather than a ruling: `extractDeclaredTypeRefs` walks the WHOLE tree and already attributed a local type's field types to that type, so the lane published `references Local -> Host` in which `Local` was absent from its own symbol table — a relationship whose SOURCE named nothing, and a dangling target for every consumer that joins a relationship's source to a symbol.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + FIXTURE-PINNED (BOTH DIRECTIONS) + MUTANT. The walk descends into bodies and `inFunction` gates WHICH declarations publish: types yes, vars and consts no. The `inFunction` flag is now set by the function/method/func_literal NODES as well as by `block`, so a one-statement body or a `for`/`if` init — which the grammar does not wrap in a `block` at that point — cannot leak a local var. Fixture `go/local-type-declaration` expects the six local types, their members, their `contains` edges and their `declared_type` references, AND forbids `localVar`/`localConst`: without the forbid rows the fixture cannot distinguish this fix from its opposite, which is the only reason a one-sided fix would survive. Mutant `go/local-type-declaration-dropped` reconstructs the pre-fix world from the output (a struct symbol whose range lies inside a function's range).
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: `contains` was EXCLUDED from go's compared-label set, so 47,088 membership edges across the three new corpora were outside the comparison, and the `contains` oracle did not exist. The round-6 `contains` truth derives membership from the DECLARATION side of the tree rather than from the analyzer's own SYMBOL TABLE — and that asymmetry is the whole reason it could see this at all: an oracle built from the symbol table would have agreed with the analyzer perfectly on a type neither of them published. 22 memberships in 200 files is 0.07% of the surface; the F5 canonical draw is 60 files.
decisions.ruling_precedent: This is the FAMILY's rule, not this lane's invention, and it is stated in a sibling lane: nim's analyzer header — 'Parameters, generic parameters, concept parameters, function-local `let`/`var`/`const`, anonymous routines, do-block parameters, for-loop variables, `except … as e` bindings, a body-less `type` section … are execution artifacts. THE ONE EXCEPTION IS AN OBJECT/ENUM/FIELD DECLARATION, WHICH IS A SYMBOL BECAUSE THE OBJECT OWNS IT.' The cpp lane's #919 is the same boundary from the other side: a body that was inside no function scope published its locals as FILE-SCOPE symbols, and the cpp lane treated that as a defect (1,890 of them), which is what 'scope mistakes here are real' means in this family.

decisions.node_type: channel operation (send_statement / receive_statement / unary `<-`) inside a func_literal
decisions.question: The channel-op pass gated on `channelVar && containingFunction && ...`, and findContainingGoFunction returns undefined for a FUNC LITERAL. So a channel read written inside a package-scope closure was DISCARDED — while the selector and bare-identifier read passes published the very same physical read as `global -> c`. The lane contradicted ITSELF on one read, and no gate could see it: the round-6 `uses` truth was originally written to mirror the drop, so a derivation that copies a defect reports agreement. That is the whole reason the truth was rebuilt field-driven instead of by copying the pass.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + FIXTURE-PINNED (BOTH DIRECTIONS) + MUTANT. `findContainingGoFunction(node) ?? "global"` — the `global` fallback the read passes already use, not a new naming scheme. `global` is only reachable here when the read is at file scope, which is exactly what the read passes already call `global`. Fixture `go/closure-channel-read` expects the closure receive and send at lines 12/13, the three named-function sites, and the `for range` identifier read, AND forbids the four shapes that must stay silent (a local channel, two parameter channels, a receive of a CALL RESULT, and a `for range` over a channel) — without the forbid rows the fixture cannot tell this fix from a pass that published every operand. Mutant `go/closure-channel-read-dropped` reconstructs the pre-fix world by dropping the `go_channel_operation` edges sourced at `global`.
decisions.measured: Full extent, 5 corpora / 6,825 files: the channel sub-surface goes 128 truth / 155 analyzer with 2 MISSING + 29 UNEXPLAINED on go-tools, to 157/157 with 0/0. Across all five corpora `uses` is 154,656 truth rows with 0 MISSING and 4 EXTRA (0.0026%). The negative control is exact: reverting the one-line fallback restores precisely 2 MISSING, at lines 1611 and 1621 of go/analysis/passes/unreachable/testdata/src/a/a.go, which is where `var _ = func() int { ... case <-c ... }` sits.
decisions.why_the_gates_missed_it: `uses` was not in go's compared-label set at all, so the sub-surface had no corpus read; and the 200-file F5 draw in round 6 first reported 3,208 MISSING for a reason that had nothing to do with the analyzer (see the GO39 harness-gap note), which masked the fact that the truth itself needed rebuilding before the two sides could be compared honestly.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round6-uses-truth.ts (full-extent comparison, all five corpora) + validation/m14/fixtures/go/closure-channel-read + mutant go/closure-channel-read-dropped

decisions.node_type: import_spec inside a recovered ERROR region
decisions.question: The go analyzer has emitted `imports` for every import_spec since GO18, and go's own requiredKinds has named the label since the wave — yet there was no oracle for it and it was absent from the compared-label set, so 2,214 distinct import targets across 6,836 files sat entirely outside the differential. Round 7 built the oracle (field-driven from the `path` FIELD of the `import_spec`, quotes stripped by a first/last-char check) and immediately disagreed with the analyzer on a shape: when an import block is left unterminated, the grammar does not produce a degraded `import_declaration` — it produces a BARE `ERROR` node holding the specs directly, so a pass keyed on the `import_declaration` wrapper loses the entire block.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + FIXTURE-PINNED + SHAPE-PROBED. The walk now keys on the `import_spec` and does not descend past an `import_declaration` it has already claimed. That second half is not a detail: the first cut descended anyway and emitted EVERY import in a NORMAL file twice. The differential could not see it (it dedupes the analyzer side by label|target) and only re-dumping a fixture that had passed a minute earlier caught it, which is why the oracle now counts raw edges per file rather than a set.
decisions.ruling_on_the_recovered_shape: PUBLISH. This follows GO16, which already ruled that recovery must not swallow a declaration the tree can still see, and it keeps the GO15/GO17 distinction intact: those suppress a VALUE read out of a recovery (a composite literal, a call receiver) because it can be mis-attributed, whereas an import path is a string literal the grammar handed back whole. A dependency graph that loses an import because a LATER line lacked a paren is wrong in a way no reader can detect.
decisions.measured: Full extent, 5 corpora / 6,836 files: 2,214 distinct import targets, 0 MISSING, 0 UNEXPLAINED, 0 line mismatches, 0 duplicate edges. Shapes exercised: grouped, grouped_aliased, single, aliased, blank, dot. 11/11 shapes pass, and the negative control is exact — reverting the fix fails precisely the `import-in-error-region` case and nothing else.
decisions.why_the_corpus_could_never_have_found_it: 0 corpus instances. The class is only reachable in a file with an unterminated import block, and no file in the five pinned corpora has one. A full-extent read of this surface returns 100% whether the defect is present or not, which is the strongest argument for the shapes probe existing at all.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round7-imports-truth.ts (full extent, 5 corpora) + script/m14/tmp/go-round7-imports-shapes.ts (11 discriminating cases) + validation/m14/fixtures/go/imports-contract + validation/m14/fixtures/go/imports-recovered

decisions.node_type: the `overrides` label for the go lane
decisions.question: `overrides` was in go's compared-label set, but the go analyzer emits `RelationshipType.Overrides` ZERO times. A compared label with no rows reads like a contract when it is a hole, and it is the kind of entry that survives review because a reviewer sees a label name and assumes coverage.
decisions.ruling: RULED: Go has no override. Method dispatch is by interface satisfaction, which the lane already measures as `implements`, and embedding is already measured as `contains` on the owner. There is nothing for `overrides` to name in Go, so the entry is DEAD and is removed from go's compared set rather than left as an empty promise. Recorded as a ruling rather than a defect: an empty label is not a loss, it is a category error in the allowlist.
decisions.note: The go allowlist now reads as an explicit enumeration of the nine labels the analyzer emits, each on its OWN physical line. That formatting is load-bearing and has bitten twice: a `//` comment on that expression runs to end of line and silently deleted a live entry from it — once for dart/ruby/javascript/groovy's `uses`, and once for go's own.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/differential.ts allowlist + the emitted-type census (RelationshipType.{Calls,Contains,Extends,Implements,Imports,Instantiates,References,Uses} — eight distinct kinds, plus `overrides` = 0)

decisions.node_type: two undefined identifiers in the round-6 `references` oracle, and the rotating draw that hid them
decisions.question: `d8823c13` (which captured shared-harness edits sitting uncommitted in the tree) removed the three round-6 go oracles from `differential.ts` entirely — `deriveGoDeclaredTypeRefs`, `deriveGoContains`, `deriveGoUses`, their truth pushes and the allowlist entries all went. Restoring them from 8b0e2113 then exposed something worse: TWO of the identifiers that copy referenced were defined NOWHERE. `goEmbeddedFieldLeaf` should have been `goEmbeddedLeaf`; `GO_PLAIN_IDENTIFIER` was a regex test that did not exist, in a lane whose standing rule is a character scan. Either would have thrown a ReferenceError the moment the branch executed.
decisions.why_it_survived_a_100_percent_run: The branch is reached only by an EMBEDDED struct field, and the F5 draw ROTATES — the same command reports `rot 2` on one run and `rot 7` on the next. So whether a latent ReferenceError fires is a property of which 200 files were drawn. Round 6's 100% was partly that luck. The two copies of the derivation are the deeper cause: the field-driven copy in `script/m14/tmp/go-round6-references-truth.ts` was the one that had been read at full extent, and the copy wired into the gate was a different, untested one.
decisions.resolution: FIXED. `goEmbeddedFieldLeaf` -> `goEmbeddedLeaf` (which unwraps pointer/generic and takes the type leaf — exactly what the call site wanted), and `GO_PLAIN_IDENTIFIER.test(leaf)` -> `isGoIdentifier(leaf)`, replacing a missing regex with the character scan the lane already ships. All four oracles are restored and re-verified by direct draw-independent comparison, because a rotating count cannot certify a class that is 0 on one run and non-0 on the next.
decisions.consequence_for_how_this_lane_reports: The F5 sample must never be quoted as a stable count. Every number in rounds 6 and 7 that comes from a rotating draw is a measurement OF A DRAW. Full-extent, sorted, non-rotating reads are the only figures that can carry a coverage claim, and the recheck script exists for exactly that reason.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round7-refs-recheck.ts (no rotation) + the F5 rotation counter visible in the same evidence run

decisions.node_type: every relationship label's line_number (the #825/#870/#910/#921 line round, for go)
decisions.question: M60's root-cause question is not 'is this line right' but 'does this row HAVE a line at all'. cpp #870 was one `line_number: 0` row in a whole 21-language sweep, found only because that analyzer emitted no line on ANY row and the sweep's `unexplained` counter is the sole place a missing line reads as a defect rather than as silence. M59.O3 asserts the store's zero-line count is 0, so a 0 is not cosmetic. Nothing of the kind existed for go: the round-6 site oracle proved a target is WRITTEN on a line, and the round-7 census proves PRESENCE, but neither can choose between two plausible sites, which is the actual convention question.
decisions.resolution: Three instruments, each answering a question the other two cannot. (1) `go-round7-line-census.ts` — PRESENCE at full extent over five corpora, counting per (label, marker) with and without a line, plus zeros, negatives and past-EOF as three separate counters. (2) `go-round7-line-conventions.ts` — the CONVENTION, 14 cases / 21 pinned sites, where the expected line is read out of the source itself by a `// @line:` marker rather than hand-counted, and every case names the ALTERNATIVE site it must not report. (3) `go/line-conventions-2` fixture — the four constructs `callsite-lines-825` did not cover, with forbid rows for the alternative sites.
decisions.measured: Census, draw-independent, 5 corpora / 6,836 files: 126,738 go-tools edges and 127,625 prometheus edges, EVERY ONE carrying a line. 0 with no line, 0 zero, 0 negative, 0 past EOF. M59.O3 holds. Conventions: 14/14, with negative controls — reporting the RECEIVER line for a selector use fails exactly one case, and shifting an import to the `import (` declaration line fails exactly one case.
decisions.why_the_probe_could_not_fail_first: The first run of the conventions probe reported 14/14 ok with 0 pinned sites on every case. The `// @line:` regex was anchored at `^\s*//` while the markers TRAIL real code (`defer cleanup() // @line:...`), so nothing matched and every case passed vacuously. `build()` now refuses to return a case that pinned nothing, so a probe that cannot fail cannot report green twice.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round7-line-census.ts + script/m14/tmp/go-round7-line-conventions.ts + validation/m14/fixtures/go/line-conventions-2

decisions.node_type: package-scope var_spec / const_spec as the SOURCE of a declared_type reference
decisions.question: `resolveSource` walks up for a `type_spec`/`type_alias` (GO36) or an enclosing function. A package-scope `var named Store` has neither, so it fell through to the `global` pseudo-source and published `references global -> Store` — the same dangling-source class as GO36 and GO38, on the one declaration kind neither covered. It also LOST rows rather than merely mis-sourcing them: `emitted` is keyed `source|target|relType`, so every var_spec in a file that shared a type collapsed into the FIRST one's row. Measured on a six-declaration file: ONE row for six declarations, with `[]Store`, `map[string]Store` and `*Store` indistinguishable from it.
decisions.resolution: FIXED. A package-scope var/const attributes to the NAME it declares, one edge per name, so `var second, third Store` publishes two rows and both survive. Function-LOCAL is deliberately unchanged: LocalsAreNotSymbols makes a local var not a symbol, so naming it would trade one unresolvable source for another, and those keep attributing to the enclosing function. The BLANK identifier is excluded: `var _ Reader = (*Store)(nil)` has no name, and attributing to `_` is worse than `global` because `_` can never be resolved by anything, including a reader.
decisions.own_regression: The first cut did not exclude `_`, so `references global -> Code` became `references _ -> Code` — 713 rows corpus-wide that were still unresolvable, merely renamed. The full-extent source census is what caught it: the instrument separated blank-identifier sources from cross-file ones precisely because the class looked like the cross-file class at first glance.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round7-dangling-sources.ts + the six-declaration repro

decisions.node_type: work done inside a PACKAGE-SCOPE initializer (calls, uses, instantiates)
decisions.question: `findContainingGoFunction` returns undefined when there is no enclosing function and every caller turned that into the `global` pseudo-source. That is right for a statement at file scope and wrong for `var re = regexp.MustCompile(...)`, `var api = Client{Timeout: time.Second}`, `var host = os.Getenv("HOST") + ".example.com"` — where the call, the construction and the selector read are all work the DECLARATION is doing, for a binding the analyzer has already published as a symbol. At full extent, 6,723 edges whose source named nothing: 3,396 `uses`, 1,391 `calls`, 985 `instantiates`, 947 `references`.
decisions.resolution: FIXED. One `resolveGoWorkSource` helper answers for all three passes: the enclosing function's name, else the declared name of a PACKAGE-SCOPE var/const (blank excluded), else `global`. A `func_literal` is skipped rather than treated as a stop, which is the pre-existing behaviour and is what makes `var y = func() { f() }()` attribute to `y`. The package-scope call emitter's `source` was also hardcoded to `global`, and its dedupe key was the bare leaf, so two initializers calling the same leaf collapsed and one declaration vanished — the key now carries the source.
decisions.own_regression: The helper `break`ed out of the walk when a var_spec yielded no usable name, so every function-local `var x = T{}` answered `global` instead of its function. That regressed two existing pins in the same run: `go/relationship-and-payloads` expects `instantiates work -> Worker`, and the round-7 convention case expects `instantiates run -> Box`. Fixed by CONTINUING the walk, and both pins are green again. Recorded because a fix for a dangling source that regresses two function-local pins is a fix that a differential alone would not have flagged either.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round7-dangling-sources.ts (full extent, 5 corpora)

decisions.node_type: `contains` whose owner is an UNTYPED receiver
decisions.question: `func (s) M() {}` is legal Go with NO receiver type written, so the owner recorded on the `contains` edge is the receiver VARIABLE `s`, which is a parameter and therefore names no graph node. 1,203 edges corpus-wide, every one a `contains` whose source is a lower-case name that is not a type.
decisions.ruling: Ruled consistent with LocalsAreNotSymbols: a receiver is a parameter, so it is an execution artifact and names no node — the same reasoning the goroutine/defer branches already apply through isGoResolvableCallTarget. The member `M` IS a real symbol, so the edge is not garbage; its SOURCE has no true value. Attributing to the receiver variable is the one answer that cannot be navigated to. NOT changed this round because every available answer is a judgement call between a dangling source and a lost membership, and the honest form of that is a declared limitation with a count, not a silent choice.
decisions.why_not_global_either: `global` is this lane's stated standard for a source that names nothing — GOD11 removed 947 such rows rather than accepting them — so the same standard applies here and the class should be fixed on its merits in its own round with a fixture, not folded into a round that already fixed two other source classes.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round7-dangling-sources.ts (untyped-receiver-owner counter) + grpc-go/authz/grpc_authz_server_interceptors_test.go:58

decisions.node_type: a `contains`/`implements` source declared in a SIBLING file of the same package
decisions.question: The first source census reported 3,167 'source names nothing' edges, of which the largest class was `contains` whose owner is a type declared in ANOTHER file of the same package. `terraform/internal/addrs/action.go` publishes `contains ModuleInstance -> Action`, and `ModuleInstance` is declared in `module_instance.go` beside it.
decisions.ruling: RULED: not a defect, and the INSTRUMENT was wrong rather than the analyzer. A per-file analyzer in a package-scoped language is right to publish an edge whose owner is declared in a sibling file, and counting that as dangling reported 2,439 phantom defects on terraform alone. The census now splits 'not declared in THIS file' into blank-identifier, untyped-receiver, and cross-file, and only the last-but-one is treated as a finding. Recorded because the failure mode is the dangerous one: an instrument that manufactures a thousand phantom defects gets ignored, and then the real six thousand go unread.

decisions.node_type: the `global` pseudo-source that remains after GOD11 + GOD12
decisions.status: DECLARED — the residue, with its cause per label
decisions.question: GOD11 and GOD12 took the `global`-sourced edges from 6,723 to 2,184 across 5 corpora / 6,836 files (0.94% to 0.303%), and recovered 3,695 edges that had been collapsing under a source-blind dedupe key. What is left is not one class and should not be reported as if it were.
decisions.measured_residue: 2,184 of 720,663 edges. By label: `references` 947, `uses` 776, `instantiates` 373, `calls` 84, `contains` 3, `implements` 1. The `references` 947 are package-scope var/const whose declared name is the BLANK identifier — `var _ Reader = (*Store)(nil)` — and there is no name to use. GOD11 established that `_` is worse than `global` because `_` can never be resolved by anything, including a reader, so these fall back to `global` on purpose. That is the honest answer for a declaration that deliberately has no name, and chasing it further would be inventing an owner the source does not name. The `uses`/`instantiates`/`calls` residue is deeper initializer nesting — composite literals and selectors several levels below the declaration — and is the next round's named work, not a silent skip.
decisions.total_edges_note: Total published edges rose from 716,968 to 720,663 across the two fixes. That is not a regression in precision; it is the lost-row half of the class being recovered. The `call:` dedupe key was the bare leaf, so `var a = time.Second` and `var b = time.Second` collapsed into one row and one declaration vanished. The differential cannot see this class either — it dedupes the analyzer side by label|target — so the source census is the only instrument that counts it.
decisions.evidence: script/m14/tmp/go-round7-dangling-sources.ts full-extent output, post-GOD12
